question: Who built the ark, and who told him to build it?
expected_answer: God told Noah to make an ark of gopher wood, and Noah did all that God commanded him (Gen.6.13-14, Gen.6.22).

expected_contexts.text: And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.

question: How did David defeat Goliath?
expected_answer: David slung a stone that sank into the Philistine's forehead, prevailing over Goliath with a sling and a stone and no sword in his hand (1Sam.17.49-50).

expected_contexts.text: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.
So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.

question: Where was Jesus born?
expected_answer: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea, the city of David; Mary laid him in a manger because there was no room in the inn (Matt.2.1, Luke.2.4, Luke.2.7).

expected_contexts.text: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,
And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:)
And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.

question: Which disciple denied Jesus three times before the cock crowed?
expected_answer: Peter. Jesus foretold that before the cock crew he would deny him thrice, and after it happened Peter remembered and wept bitterly (Matt.26.34, Matt.26.75).

expected_contexts.text: Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.

question: Who betrayed Jesus, and for how much?
expected_answer: Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, agreed with the chief priests to deliver Jesus for thirty pieces of silver (Matt.26.14-15).

expected_contexts.text: Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests,
And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.

question: Who committed the first murder recorded in the Bible?
expected_answer: Cain rose up against his brother Abel in the field and slew him; afterwards he asked, "Am I my brother's keeper?" (Gen.4.8-9).

expected_contexts.text: And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
And the Lord said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?

question: Who was thrown into the den of lions, and how did he survive?
expected_answer: Daniel was cast into the den of lions at King Darius's command; God sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths (Dan.6.16, Dan.6.22).

expected_contexts.text: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel, Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.
My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.

question: How were the Ten Commandments given to Moses?
expected_answer: God spoke these words, and on Mount Sinai gave Moses two tables of testimony, tables of stone written with the finger of God; later the ten commandments were written again on tables (Exod.20.1, Exod.31.18, Exod.34.28).

expected_contexts.text: And God spake all these words, saying,
And he gave unto Moses, when he had made an end of communing with him upon mount Sinai, two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God.
And he was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights; he did neither eat bread, nor drink water. And he wrote upon the tables the words of the covenant, the ten commandments.

question: What did Solomon ask God for when God appeared to him in a dream?
expected_answer: Solomon asked for an understanding heart to judge the people and discern between good and bad; God gave him a wise and understanding heart (1Kgs.3.9, 1Kgs.3.12).

expected_contexts.text: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?
Behold, I have done according to thy words: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee.

question: What was Jesus' first miracle according to John's Gospel?
expected_answer: At the wedding in Cana of Galilee Jesus turned water into wine; John calls this the beginning of his miracles (John.2.9, John.2.11).

expected_contexts.text: When the ruler of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and knew not whence it was: (but the servants which drew the water knew;) the governor of the feast called the bridegroom,
This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him.

question: How long did it rain during Noah's flood?
expected_answer: The rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights (Gen.7.12, Gen.7.17).

expected_contexts.text: And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
And the flood was forty days upon the earth; and the waters increased, and bare up the ark, and it was lift up above the earth.

question: What was the name of the son Sarah bore to Abraham, and how old was Abraham?
expected_answer: Sarah bore Abraham a son in his old age and he called him Isaac; Abraham was a hundred years old (Gen.21.2-3, Gen.21.5).

expected_contexts.text: For Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.
And Abraham called the name of his son that was born unto him, whom Sarah bare to him, Isaac.
And Abraham was an hundred years old, when his son Isaac was born unto him.

question: Who interpreted Pharaoh's dreams, and what did they mean?
expected_answer: Joseph, saying the answer comes from God, interpreted them as seven years of great plenty followed by seven years of famine (Gen.41.15-16, Gen.41.29-30).

expected_contexts.text: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret it: and I have heard say of thee, that thou canst understand a dream to interpret it.
And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.
Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt:
And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land;

question: What happened to the walls of Jericho?
expected_answer: When the people shouted with a great shout at the sound of the trumpets, the wall fell down flat and they took the city (Josh.6.20).

expected_contexts.text: So the people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets: and it came to pass, when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, and the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city.

question: What was the secret of Samson's strength?
expected_answer: He was a Nazarite from birth and no razor had come on his head; if he were shaven his strength would go from him (Judg.16.17).

expected_contexts.text: That he told her all his heart, and said unto her, There hath not come a razor upon mine head; for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother’s womb: if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man.

question: Who baptized Jesus, and what happened at his baptism?
expected_answer: John baptized Jesus at the Jordan; the Spirit of God descended like a dove and a voice from heaven said, "This is my beloved Son" (Matt.3.13, Matt.3.16-17).

expected_contexts.text: Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.
And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:
And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

question: What happened to Saul on the road to Damascus?
expected_answer: A light from heaven shone round him, he fell to the earth and heard a voice: "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" — it was Jesus (Acts.9.3-5).

expected_contexts.text: And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven:
And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

question: Which prophet was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind?
expected_answer: Elijah; a chariot of fire and horses of fire parted him and Elisha, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven (2Kgs.2.11).

expected_contexts.text: And it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

question: Who climbed a sycomore tree to see Jesus?
expected_answer: Zacchaeus, a rich chief tax collector who was short, ran ahead and climbed a sycomore tree (Luke.19.2, Luke.19.4).

expected_contexts.text: And, behold, there was a man named Zaccheus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.
And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.

question: What did Moses see at the burning bush and what was he told?
expected_answer: The angel of the Lord appeared in a flame of fire out of a bush that burned but was not consumed; God called to Moses and told him to put off his shoes, for the place was holy ground (Exod.3.2, Exod.3.4-5).

expected_contexts.text: And the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
And when the Lord saw that he turned aside to see, God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I.
And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

question: What did Esau sell to Jacob, and for what?
expected_answer: Esau sold his birthright to Jacob for bread and pottage of lentiles (Gen.25.33-34).

expected_contexts.text: And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob.
Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright.

question: How many loaves and fish did Jesus use to feed the five thousand?
expected_answer: Five loaves and two fishes; about five thousand men, besides women and children, ate (Matt.14.17, Matt.14.19, Matt.14.21).

expected_contexts.text: And they say unto him, We have here but five loaves, and two fishes.

And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.
And they that had eaten were about five thousand men, beside women and children.

question: Why were Joseph's brothers jealous, and what did they do to him?
expected_answer: Israel loved Joseph more than all his children and made him a coat of many colours; the brothers sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver (Gen.37.3, Gen.37.28).

expected_contexts.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.
Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.

question: According to the Quran, who refused to prostrate before Adam, and why?
expected_answer: Iblis refused out of pride; he said, "I am better than him. Thou createdst me of fire while him Thou didst create of mud" (Q002.2.34, Q007.7.12).

expected_contexts.text: And when We said unto the angels: Prostrate yourselves before Adam, they fell prostrate, all save Iblis. He demurred through pride, and so became a disbeliever.
He said: What hindered thee that thou didst not fall prostrate when I bade thee? (Iblis) said: I am better than him. Thou createdst me of fire while him Thou didst create of mud.

question: How long did Noah stay among his people according to the Quran?
expected_answer: A thousand years save fifty years, i.e. 950 years, before the flood engulfed them (Q029.29.14).

expected_contexts.text: And verily we sent Noah (as Our messenger) unto his folk, and he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years; and the flood engulfed them, for they were wrong-doers.

question: Where did Noah's ship come to rest according to the Quran?
expected_answer: On (the mount) Al-Judi, after the earth swallowed its water and the water subsided (Q011.11.44).

expected_contexts.text: And it was said: O earth! Swallow thy water and, O sky! be cleared of clouds! And the water was made to subside. And the commandment was fulfilled. And it (the ship) came to rest upon (the mount) Al-Judi and it was said: A far removal for wrongdoing folk!

question: How long did the sleepers of the cave stay in their cave?
expected_answer: Three hundred years, and nine more were added (Q018.18.25).

expected_contexts.text: And (it is said) they tarried in their Cave three hundred years and add nine.

question: Who raised the foundations of the House (the Kaaba) according to the Quran?
expected_answer: Abraham and Ishmael raised the foundations of the House, praying that Allah accept it from them (Q002.2.127).

expected_contexts.text: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, (Abraham prayed): Our Lord! Accept from us (this duty). Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Hearer, the Knower.

question: What happened when Solomon and his army reached the Valley of the Ants?
expected_answer: An ant warned the others to enter their dwellings lest Solomon and his armies crush them unknowingly; Solomon smiled at her speech and prayed to be thankful (Q027.27.18-19).

expected_contexts.text: Till, when they reached the Valley of the Ants, an ant exclaimed: O ants! Enter your dwellings lest Solomon and his armies crush you, unperceiving.

And (Solomon) smiled, laughing at her speech, and said: My Lord, arouse me to be thankful for Thy favour wherewith Thou hast favoured me and my parents, and to do good that shall be pleasing unto Thee, and include me in (the number of) Thy righteous slaves.

question: In Surah Maryam, what did the infant Jesus say from the cradle?
expected_answer: When Mary pointed to him, he spoke: "Lo! I am the slave of Allah. He hath given me the Scripture and hath appointed me a Prophet" (Q019.19.29-30).

expected_contexts.text: Then she pointed to him. They said: How can we talk to one who is in the cradle, a young boy?
He spake: Lo! I am the slave of Allah. He hath given me the Scripture and hath appointed me a Prophet,

question: In which month was the Quran revealed, and what is commanded in it?
expected_answer: The month of Ramadan; whoever is present should fast the month, while the sick or travellers make up the days later (Q002.2.185).

expected_contexts.text: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind, and clear proofs of the guidance, and the Criterion (of right and wrong). And whosoever of you is present, let him fast the month, and whosoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast the same) number of other days. Allah desireth for you ease; He desireth not hardship for you; and (He desireth) that ye should complete the period, and that ye should magnify Allah for having guided you, and that peradventure ye may be thankful.

question: What was Moses' mother inspired to do with her baby according to the Quran?
expected_answer: To suckle him and, when she feared for him, cast him into the river without fear or grief, with the promise that he would be returned to her and made a messenger (Q028.28.7).

expected_contexts.text: And We inspired the mother of Moses, saying: Suckle him and, when thou fearest for him, then cast him into the river and fear not nor grieve. Lo! We shall bring him back unto thee and shall make him (one) of Our messengers.

question: What did Allah command the fire when Abraham was thrown into it?
expected_answer: "O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham" (Q021.21.69).

expected_contexts.text: We said: O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham,

question: What news did the hoopoe bring to Solomon?
expected_answer: Solomon noticed the hoopoe was absent; it returned with sure tidings from Sheba of a woman ruling over a people, given abundance of all things, with a mighty throne (Q027.27.20, Q027.27.22-23).

expected_contexts.text: And he sought among the birds and said: How is it that I see not the hoopoe, or is he among the absent?
But he was not long in coming, and he said: I have found out (a thing) that thou apprehendest not, and I come unto thee from Sheba with sure tidings.
Lo! I found a woman ruling over them, and she hath been given (abundance) of all things, and hers is a mighty throne.

question: How does the Quran describe Muhammad's position among the prophets?
expected_answer: Muhammad is not the father of any man among them, but the messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets (Q033.33.40).

expected_contexts.text: Muhammad is not the father of any man among you, but he is the messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets; and Allah is ever Aware of all things.

question: What does Surah 97 say about the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr)?
expected_answer: The Quran was revealed on that night, and the Night of Power is better than a thousand months (Q097.97.1, Q097.97.3).

expected_contexts.text: Lo! We revealed it on the Night of Predestination.
The Night of Power is better than a thousand months.

question: What happened when Moses met his Lord according to the Quran?
expected_answer: At the holy valley of Tuwa he was told to take off his shoes (Q020.20.12); at the appointed tryst Moses asked to see Allah and was told "Thou wilt not see Me" but to look at the mountain (Q007.7.143).

expected_contexts.text: Lo! I, even I, am thy Lord, So take off thy shoes, for lo! thou art in the holy valley of Tuwa.

And when Moses came to Our appointed tryst and his Lord had spoken unto him, he said: My Lord! Show me (Thy Self), that I may gaze upon Thee. He said: Thou wilt not see Me, but gaze upon the mountain! If it stand still in its place, then thou wilt see Me. And when his Lord revealed (His) glory to the mountain He sent it crashing down. And Moses fell down senseless. And when he woke he said: Glory unto Thee! I turn unto Thee repentant, and I am the first of (true) believers.

question: What did Joseph's brothers do to him, and how did he respond to the woman who tried to seduce him, according to Surah Yusuf?
expected_answer: His brothers agreed to put him in the depth of the pit (Q012.12.15); when the woman of the house bolted the doors and invited him, he said "I seek refuge in Allah!" (Q012.12.23).

expected_contexts.text: Then, when they led him off, and were of one mind that they should place him in the depth of the pit, We inspired in him: Thou wilt tell them of this deed of theirs when they know (thee) not.

And she, in whose house he was, asked of him an evil act. She bolted the doors and said: Come! He said: I seek refuge in Allah! Lo! he is my lord, who hath treated me honourably. Lo! wrong-doers never prosper.

question: What does the Bible teach about forgiving others?
expected_answer: If you forgive men their trespasses your heavenly Father will forgive you, but not if you refuse (Matt.6.14-15); forgive not seven times but seventy times seven (Matt.18.21-22); be kind and forgive one another as God for Christ's sake forgave you (Eph.4.32).

expected_contexts.text: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?
Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.
And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.

question: How should Christians treat their enemies?
expected_answer: Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them that despitefully use you (Matt.5.44, Luke.6.27-28).

expected_contexts.text: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;
But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you,
Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.

question: What attitude does the Bible ask for when giving?
expected_answer: Give as you purpose in your heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loves a cheerful giver (2Cor.9.7); give in secret, not letting the left hand know what the right does (Matt.6.3); it is more blessed to give than to receive (Acts.20.35).

expected_contexts.text: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.
But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:
I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

question: What does the Bible say about patience?
expected_answer: Be patient in tribulation and continue instant in prayer (Rom.12.12); be patient like the husbandman waiting for the fruit of the earth (Jas.5.7); let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire (Jas.1.4).

expected_contexts.text: Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer;

Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain.
But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.

question: What does the Bible say about worry and anxiety?
expected_answer: Take no thought for the morrow (Matt.6.34); be careful for nothing but bring your requests to God in prayer with thanksgiving (Phil.4.6); cast all your care upon him, for he careth for you (1Pet.5.7).

expected_contexts.text: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

question: What does the Bible teach about pride and humility?
expected_answer: Pride goeth before destruction (Prov.16.18); God resisteth the proud but giveth grace unto the humble (Jas.4.6); in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves (Phil.2.3); walk humbly with thy God (Mic.6.8).

expected_contexts.text: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.
Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.
He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the Lord require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?

question: What does the Bible say about honouring parents?
expected_answer: Honour thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be long (Exod.20.12); children, obey your parents in the Lord — the first commandment with promise (Eph.6.1-2).

expected_contexts.text: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.
Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.
Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)

question: How does 1 Corinthians 13 describe love?
expected_answer: It suffers long and is kind, envies not, vaunts not itself (1Cor.13.4); beareth, believeth, hopeth and endureth all things (1Cor.13.7); of faith, hope and charity, the greatest is charity (1Cor.13.13). KJV renders love as "charity".

expected_contexts.text: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,
Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.
And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.

question: How does the Bible define faith?
expected_answer: Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen; without faith it is impossible to please God (Heb.11.1, Heb.11.6).

expected_contexts.text: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

question: What does the Bible warn about wealth and money?
expected_answer: The love of money is the root of all evil (1Tim.6.10); ye cannot serve God and mammon (Matt.6.24); it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God (Matt.19.24).

expected_contexts.text: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

question: What does the Bible say about caring for the poor?
expected_answer: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord (Prov.19.17); whatever you did to the least of my brethren you did unto me (Matt.25.40); pure religion is to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction (Jas.1.27).

expected_contexts.text: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.

question: What does the Bible teach about anger?
expected_answer: Be ye angry and sin not; let not the sun go down upon your wrath (Eph.4.26); be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath, for man's wrath works not God's righteousness (Jas.1.19-20).

expected_contexts.text: Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath:
Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.

question: What does the Bible say about work and laziness?
expected_answer: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways and be wise (Prov.6.6); if any would not work, neither should he eat (2Thess.3.10); whatever you do, do it heartily as to the Lord (Col.3.23).

expected_contexts.text: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:
For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men;

question: What does the Bible say about the power of words and the tongue?
expected_answer: Death and life are in the power of the tongue (Prov.18.21); let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth (Eph.4.29); the tongue is a little member that boasts great things, like a little fire kindling a great matter (Jas.3.5).

expected_contexts.text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers.
Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!

question: How should strangers and foreigners be treated according to the Bible?

question: Compare the flood story of Noah in the Bible and the Quran.
expected_answer: Both tell of a flood and the ark resting on a mountain: the Bible has forty days of rain and the ark resting on the mountains of Ararat (Gen.7.12, Gen.8.4); the Quran says the ship came to rest on al-Judi (Q011.11.44) and that Noah stayed among his people 950 years (Q029.29.14).

And verily we sent Noah (as Our messenger) unto his folk, and he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years; and the flood engulfed them, for they were wrong-doers.

question: How do the Bible and the Quran describe the parting of the sea and Pharaoh's fate?
expected_answer: In Exodus Moses stretched out his hand, the Lord divided the waters and the sea covered Pharaoh's host (Exod.14.21, Exod.14.28); in the Quran Moses struck the sea with his staff and it parted (Q026.26.63), Pharaoh declared belief as he drowned and his body was preserved as a sign (Q010.10.90, Q010.10.92).

expected_contexts.text: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the Lord caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.
And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.
Then We inspired Moses, saying: Smite the sea with thy staff. And it parted, and each part was as a mountain vast.

And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh with his hosts pursued them in rebellion and transgression, till, when the (fate of) drowning overtook him, he exclaimed: I believe that there is no Allah save Him in Whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of those who surrender (unto Him).
But this day We save thee in thy body that thou mayst be a portent for those after thee. Lo! most of mankind are heedless of Our portents.

question: Compare the annunciation to Mary in the Bible and the Quran.
expected_answer: In Luke the angel tells Mary she will conceive and bear a son named Jesus, and she asks how, since she knows not a man (Luke.1.30-31, Luke.1.34); in the Quran the messenger says he will bestow a faultless son, and Mary asks how, when no mortal has touched her (Q019.19.19-20).

expected_contexts.text: And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God.
And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS.
Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?
He said: I am only a messenger of thy Lord, that I may bestow on thee a faultless son.
She said: How can I have a son when no mortal hath touched me, neither have I been unchaste?

question: How do the Bible and the Quran describe Abraham's willingness to sacrifice his son?
expected_answer: In Genesis God tells Abraham to offer Isaac, then stops him and a ram is offered instead (Gen.22.2, Gen.22.12-13); in the Quran Abraham tells his son of a dream that he must sacrifice him, the son submits, and he is ransomed with a tremendous victim (Q037.37.102, Q037.37.107). expected_contexts.text: And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.
And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me.

And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.

And when (his son) was old enough to walk with him, (Abraham) said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Allah willing, thou shalt find me of the steadfast.
Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim.

question: Do the Bible and the Quran both say the world was created in six days?
expected_answer: Yes. The Bible says God made heaven and earth in six days and rested on the seventh (Gen.2.2, Exod.20.11); the Quran says Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days and then mounted the Throne (Q007.7.54), without mentioning rest.

He covereth the night with the day, which is in haste to follow it, and hath made the sun and the moon and the stars subservient by His command. His verily is all creation and commandment. Blessed be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds!

Then they twain ate thereof, so that their shame became apparent unto them, and they began to hide by heaping on themselves some of the leaves of the Garden. And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so went astray.

question: Compare the story of Adam's two sons (Cain and Abel) in the Bible and the Quran.
expected_answer: In Genesis Cain killed Abel and Abel's blood cried from the ground (Gen.4.8, Gen.4.10); the Quran tells of Adam's two sons whose offerings were accepted from one only, the killing, and a raven showing the killer how to hide his brother's corpse (Q005.5.27, Q005.5.30-31).
